message.content:
**Paris Get‑away Planner**  
*(Assuming a 7‑day trip, mid‑April 2025 – a lovely time for spring weather and fewer crowds than summer)*  

| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening |
|-----|---------|-----------|---------|
| **Day 1 – Arrival** | Fly into Charles de Gaulle (CDG) or Orly (ORY). Take the RER B or Orlybus to your hotel. | Check‑in, unpack, quick stroll to a nearby café for a croissant & café au lait. | Dinner at a classic bistro (e.g., **Le Comptoir du Relais**). Light walk along the Seine, maybe a river cruise to see the city lights. |
| **Day 2 – Classic Landmarks** | Breakfast at **Café de Flore** (Saint‑Germain‑des‑Près). Visit Notre‑Dame & Sainte‑Chapelle. | Lunch in the Latin Quarter. Walk to the Louvre; spend 2–3 hrs exploring the main galleries. | Dinner in the Marais; try **L’As du Fallafel** for a casual bite or **Le Mary Celeste** for cocktails. |
| **Day 3 – Montmartre & Sacré‑Coeur** | Early breakfast, then hop on Metro Line 12 to Abbesses. Explore Montmartre, artists’ square, and Sacré‑Coeur. | Lunch at a local café. Visit the Musée de Montmartre or the Espace Dalí. | Dinner at **La Maison Rose** or a wine bar in Montmartre. Optional: catch a show at the Moulin Rouge (book in advance). |
| **Day 4 – Day Trip to Versailles** | Breakfast, then take RER C to Versailles. Tour the Palace, Hall of Mirrors, and Gardens. | Picnic lunch in the gardens (pick up baguette, cheese, and wine from a local market). | Return to Paris. Light dinner near your hotel or a quick snack at a bakery. |
| **Day 5 – Modern Art & Shopping** | Breakfast, then visit Centre Pompidou. Explore contemporary art and the surrounding streets. | Lunch at **Le Georges** (restaurant on the Pompidou roof). Walk to the Palais‑Royal and its gardens. | Dinner in the 1st arrondissement; try **Le Grand Véfour** for a Michelin‑starred experience. |
| **Day 6 – Leisure & Culture** | Free morning – optional spa or hammam (e.g., **Les Bains de la Ville**). | Lunch at **Café Marly** overlooking the Louvre. Afternoon visit to Musée d’Orsay or the Rodin Museum. | Sunset cruise on the Seine (book a dinner cruise for a memorable evening). |
| **Day 7 – Departure** | Pack, last‑minute souvenir shopping (e.g., **Printemps** or **Galeries Lafayette**). | Lunch at a café near your hotel. | Head to the airport via RER or taxi. |

---

## Practical Details

### 1. Flights & Airport Transfers
| Airport | Transfer Options | Approx. Cost (per person) |
|---------|------------------|---------------------------|
| CDG | RER B to Gare du Nord (≈ €10), Orlybus to Denfert‑Rochereau (≈ €8), or private shuttle (≈ €35). | €10–€35 |
| ORY | Orlybus to Denfert‑Rochereau (≈ €8), or taxi (~€35). | €8–€35 |

> **Tip:** Book flights 3–4 months in advance for best fares. Use fare alerts on Skyscanner or Google Flights.

### 2. Accommodation
| Neighborhood | Hotel Options | Approx. Cost (per night) |
|--------------|---------------|--------------------------|
| **Le Marais** | Hôtel Caron, Hotel Henriette | €180–€250 |
| **Latin Quarter** | Hotel de la Porte Dorée, Hotel Le Six | €150–€220 |
| **Saint‑Germain** | Hôtel Le Meurice, Hôtel Plaza Athénée | €300–€500 |
| **Eiffel Tower area** | Pullman Paris Tour Eiffel, Hotel Eiffel Seine | €200–€350 |

> **Tip:** Book a hotel with free cancellation. Consider Airbnb for a more local feel, especially if traveling with family.

### 3. Transportation Within Paris
| Mode | Cost (per ride) | Notes |
|------|-----------------|-------|
| Metro/Bus | €1.90 single ticket | Unlimited 90‑min pass (€7.50) |
| Navigo Week Pass | €22.80 (valid Mon‑Sun) | Unlimited travel on all public transport |
| Taxi | €2.50 base + €1.50/km | Use official taxis or rideshare apps |
| Bicycle (Velib’) | €1.75 per hour | Unlimited 30‑min rides for €5.90 |

> **Tip:** Buy a Navigo Week Pass if you’ll be traveling daily. It’s cheaper than buying single tickets.

### 4. Dining & Food Budget
| Category | Typical Cost (per person) |
|----------|---------------------------|
| Breakfast | €5–€10 |
| Lunch | €10–€20 |
| Dinner | €20–€50 (mid‑range) |
| Snacks & pastries | €3–€7 |
| Wine & drinks | €5–€15 per glass |

> **Tip:** Try local markets (Marché d’Aligre, Marché des Enfants Rouges) for fresh food and affordable meals.

### 5. Attractions & Tickets
| Attraction | Ticket Price (adult) | Booking Tip |
|------------|----------------------|-------------|
| Louvre | €17 (free on first Sunday of month) | Book online to skip the line |
| Musée d’Orsay | €14 | Book online |
| Centre Pompidou | €14 | Book online |
| Palace of Versailles | €20 (full day) | Book online |
| Eiffel Tower | €25 (3rd floor) | Book online |
| Seine Cruise | €15–€30 | Book online for better rates |

> **Tip:** Many museums offer free entry on the first Sunday of each month. Check the official websites for exact dates.

### 6. Budget Summary (per person, 7 days)
| Item | Cost (EUR) |
|------|------------|
| Flights | 350–600 |
| Accommodation | 1,200–2,000 |
| Transport (within Paris) | 100–150 |
| Food & Drink | 400–600 |
| Attractions | 200–300 |
| Miscellaneous (souvenirs, tips) | 100–200 |
| **Total** | **2,250–3,850** |

> **Tip:** Adjust the accommodation and dining choices to fit your budget. Consider staying in a 3‑star hotel or a well‑rated Airbnb to save.

### 7. Packing Checklist
- **Clothing:** Light layers (t-shirts, sweaters), comfortable walking shoes, a light jacket (April can be cool), umbrella.
- **Electronics:** Phone, charger, power adapter (Type C/E), camera.
- **Travel Essentials:** Passport, travel insurance, copies of reservations, credit cards, cash (EUR).
- **Health:** Basic first aid kit, any prescription meds, hand sanitizer.
- **Misc:** Reusable water bottle, guidebook or offline map app, notebook.

### 8. Safety & Etiquette
- **Language:** Basic French phrases help; most people speak English in tourist areas.
- **Pickpocketing:** Keep valuables in a front pocket or money belt.
- **Tipping:** 5–10 % in restaurants if service not included.
- **Public Transport:** Keep your ticket handy; inspectors may ask.

---

## Quick Reference Links

| Resource | Link |
|----------|------|
| Paris Official Tourism | https://en.parisinfo.com |
| Navigo Pass | https://www.ratp.fr/en/navigo |
| Louvre Tickets | https://www.louvre.fr/en |
| Versailles Tickets | https://www.chateauversailles.fr |
| Paris Metro Map | https://www.ratp.fr/en/plan |
| Paris Weather Forecast | https://www.accuweather.com/en/fr/paris |

---

### Final Thoughts

- **Flexibility:** Leave a day or two open for spontaneous discoveries—Paris is full of hidden cafés, street markets, and art galleries.
- **Reservations:** Book major attractions and restaurants at least 2–3 weeks in advance, especially for dinner at high‑end places.
- **Enjoy the Little Things:** A simple walk along the Canal Saint‑Martin, a picnic in Parc des Buttes‑Chaumont, or a stop at a local boulangerie can be just as memorable as the Eiffel Tower.

Have an amazing trip to Paris! If you need help booking tickets, hotels, or anything else, just let me know.
